[quote=lavinsworth_united_islands;60060039]People watch from an airport terminal, grumbling about their fights being delayed as a low rumble gets louder and louder. A few lucky travelers near the windows manage to film two large military transport aircraft touch down on both runways, stopping right on the tarmac, opening their cargo doors, and deploy a small convoy of armored vehicles all within the timespan of 5 minutes. The convoy takes a small amount of time to ensure everything is right, and they speed off to an access gate as the aircraft close their doors and taxi to a parking zone. Meeting the convoy at the access gate, two police cars blair their sirens as they speed through the streets, making a beeline for the embassy. 

The second they arrive at the police perimeter around the embassy, the turrets atop the vehicles train on the embassy, watching for a sign of threat. The other men embark from their seats, either making for buildings to take up positions on roofs, setting up a large truck that can be assumed is a mobile command center, or discerning themselves with whatever they have been trained to do. One of the men, certainly older than most of the others, walks up to the highest ranking officer he can find. Shortly after, a man who looks to be in his 20s runs over to him and says something in Llyndorran that the officer cant recognize. After the two men have a quick exchange of words, the younger man points to a badge on his vest and says in accented Roskesan ISRP officers. We need to speak to whoever is in charge here.
(Sorry that its bad, I had to do it in school and Im tired af rn -_-)[/quote]

[i][u][b]The Embassy Hostage Crisis
[/b][/u]
Smoke rolls above the rooftops. The crowds are gone. The only movement is that of the joint team of snipers, entrenched in their rooftop positions, awaiting the order.
KGI Commander was approached again by the two ISRP officers. One older, stoic, the other younger and serving as translator.

[b]KGI Commander
[/b] Youve already crossed the border with armed units and armored vehicles. Youd better explain who the hell authorized you.

The younger operative steps forward, showing a black enamel badge. 

[b]ISRP Translator[/b]
 We operate under the interlaw jurisdiction of international criminal enforcement. Were here to assist with the hostage embassy crisis.

You stiffen. That changes the calculus.  Interlaw jurisdiction gives them operational legitimacy barely, but your streets, your command still stands.

[b]KGI Commander[/b]
 You track terrorists. I protect hostages. You can observe. You can advise. But this op remains under Roskeskan control.

The ISRP nods. No argument. Theyre trained for cooperation. The older operative pulls up a portable interface. It's already displaying live internal security feeds from the embassy, marked in Roskeskan. Your intel division mustve cracked the feeds minutes ago.

[b]ISRP Agent[/b]
 Two confirmed militants. First floor in the west hallway. One has a homemade explosive vest, likely a dead-man switch. Theyve barricaded the lobby and jammed some camera access. But not all.

Footage shows one is pacing with a rifle, the other glued to the windows*

[b]KGI Commander[/b]
 The ISRP orders that we lure them in.

officers pause in confusion?*

[b]ISRP Agent[/b]
Make it look like we think there are more inside. Get loud. Shout false numbers. Act disorganized. Let them think were blind and paranoid.

You gesture to your rooftop units.

When the first pokes his head through the curtains, and drops him. Quietly. The second one will panic. Thats when we breach.

A joint special forces unit of KGI and ISRP sniper chimes in through the radio* 

Visual confirmation possible from roof 3A. Awaiting movement.

You nod. The trap is set.[/i]

[b]Sikirskian[/b] [b]Scientific[/b] [b]Directorate[/b]
Strategic Arms Division

After years of classified research, development, and technical refinement, Sikirsk has officially completed the process of nuclear weapon development. Final assembly and testing have concluded, with all core systems performing within expected parameters during subcritical tests and simulation phases.

The warhead design has passed structural and materials evaluations. All detonation mechanisms, safety systems, and triggering protocols have been validated through isolated component testing.

A live detonation was successfully conducted in a remote zone south of the Sikirskian Antarctic territory. The test confirmed full device functionality under controlled conditions. Data gathered from the detonation matched all theoretical performance models.

The uranium used in the program was sourced from [nation]Orphogron[/nation], a semi-allied state that provided material support under secure arrangements. All enrichment and weapons development were carried out exclusively by Sikirskian personnel within national facilities.

The project remained internally developed and tightly secured throughout its lifespan. No foreign technical assistance was accepted beyond raw material supply. All facilities involved have now transitioned from development to standby operational readiness.

This marks the conclusion of the development phase. No further public detail will be provided.

[quote=lavinsworth_united_islands;60062891]Mr. Achebe nods and stands up, looking slightly disappointed at the quick and somewhat bitter end to the meeting. He seems to quickly remember something, picking up something off his chair and slightly examining it as the delegation stands up. "I wish to provide at least one positive piece of this visit." He holds out his hand, a leather case inside of it. "Produced here in Ijesa. It's part of the first production run as well, so its a bit of a collectors item."

The advisor stands up along with the governor and nods to the delegation. Thank you for coming sirs. I hope this wasn't considered too big of a waste of time."

(OOC: That's a nice detail ngl)[/quote]

President Khan and Minister Shari stand up quickly when they see Representative Minister Achebe rise. When President Khan sees the leather case offered, he takes it, "thank you, I will have something delivered in return. Farewell." With that, President Khan and Minister Shari walk out of the cafe.

When President Khan reaches his APC, he hands the case to one of his guards. "This case is bugged. Discuss nothing near it and stop anyone who speaks with it nearby. Hand it back when we reach Shar." The guard nods and President Khan and Minister Shari get in their APC to return back to Shar.
